title: Emergency powers extend to "urgent" situations including an important missed opportunity
content:
A.1.9.1.1 gives two definitions with very different widths. An **emergency situation** is "any situation that would require immediate intervention to prevent initiation of Emergency Shutdown, severe peg divergence, or harm to members and users of the Ecosystem" — three concrete, severe, checkable conditions.

Then, under the Core Council's Broad Discretionary Capacity, "the Core Facilitator has broad discretion to apply the emergency-situation processes... to **urgent situations**," defined as "any situation that involves a time-sensitive matter that would need an expedited governance process, where following a standard governance cycle would be too slow, risk a larger problem, or **constitute an important missed opportunity**."

The last clause is the expansive one. The first two urgency grounds are still harm-avoidance framed loosely; "an important missed opportunity" is upside-seeking. That means the machinery built for existential threats — expedited votes, war rooms, out-of-band Executive Votes — can be invoked to move faster on something advantageous, at the discretion of a single role, with importance self-assessed.

The Atlas is aware of the cost and states it rather than hiding it. A.1.9.1.4.1 lists what the Core Facilitator must weigh before expediting: SKY holders may "miss a poll or Executive Vote due to departure from the standard governance cycles"; "expedited votes may not allow for sufficient discussion, leading to a sub-optimal solution"; there is "increased governance burden on community and increased workload for domain teams"; and — most tellingly — "frequent expedited votes may signal a lack of appreciation for a consistent and predictable governance process."

That fourth factor identifies the real risk: not any single misuse, but erosion of the expectation that governance happens on schedule. Predictability is what lets holders participate at all, and each expedited vote spends a little of it. The provision asks the facilitator to price that, while giving them sole authority to decide.
description: A.1.9.1.1 defines emergencies narrowly around shutdown, peg divergence and harm, then lets the Core Facilitator apply the same expedited processes to anything too slow for a standard cycle.
